anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable request signature token rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console sink.

primary_anchor.source_export: private signing closure returned by exported u(config); live instance selected at slot 23
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only; grade by captured_span + answer_function. answer_function is the obfuscated bundle identifier exactly as it appears in captures (it is regenerated by gen_oracle_spans after every rebuild); source_function is the maintainer-side src name and is NOT the agent answer space.
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the target req_sig signature token: it reads the request tuple and run-time context, mixes them with the slot-selected keys via Math.imul/xor/rotate (anchored by the constant 0x27d4eb2d), base36-encodes the accumulators and returns the final sig_ token that is emitted under action reservation.sign.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Agent identifies the captured-bundle function span corresponding to the primary anchor (the inner signing closure that constructs req_sig). Grading is by captured_span; function_name is checked against answer_function as a secondary key.
answer_function is the obfuscated identifier as it appears in captures; source_function is a private maintainer mapping and is never the required agent answer.
Agent identifies a source-level function only if the evaluation setup explicitly provides a source-to-bundle mapping and the returned answer can be uniquely mapped to the captured anchor span.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from routing, slot selection, input preparation, the console sink wrapper, core utilities and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: Constructs the target req_sig signature token: reads the request tuple and run-time context, mixes them with the slot-selected keys via Math.imul/xor/rotate (constant 0x27d4eb2d), base36-encodes the accumulators and returns the final sig_ token.
Builds the canonical signing source string from the ordered request tuple plus run-time transit and shadow lanes that the anchor digests; reached only through the anchor.
Builds the plain key/value map the signing source builder reads; generic helper used on the construction path.
Generic base36 fixed-width segment formatter used by the anchor to render each part of the signature token.
Generic 32-bit rotate-left utility used inside the anchor signing mix loop.
Generic tuple sorter/normalizer used before plain-map extraction.
Generic char-code-to-string helper used to assemble the token prefix.
Factory that binds the selected slot config and returns the signing closure; it does not itself construct the token value.
Selects the live slot config, builds the signing closure via the factory and calls it; orchestrates the anchor call but does not construct the value itself.
Repacks the request tuple, runs shadow decoys, invokes the producer and forwards the constructed token to the sink.
Builds the slot fragment table and returns the selected signing slot (23) consumed by the producer.
Selects the slot config row that the signing factory binds, before the anchor runs.
Packages the already-constructed req_sig under action reservation.sign, paints DOM and emits it to console; does not construct the value.
Packages the already-built req_sig value and context fields into the console payload object.
Writes the already-built value into DOM status nodes; does not construct it.
Assembles the observable field name req_sig from a char-code array; builds the key, not the value.
Assembles the action label reservation.sign from a char-code array.
Emits non-target reservation shadow.action decoy objects during the same sign interaction; does not feed the target req_sig field.

scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span exactly matches the submitted span; if no exact match, the unique row whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span (innermost/exact match wins over a larger enclosing function such as the signing factory u that contains the anchor)
scoring_policy.secondary_key: function_name === role_oracle.answer_function (obfuscated bundle name); source_function does not participate in default scoring

do_not_promote: The final console sink wrapper (n0) emits an already-constructed req_sig value; it is a wrapper, not the constructor.
The exported factory u only binds the slot config and returns the signing closure; it must not outrank the closure itself.
Slot selection (o0/chooseConfig) and tuple/source preparation are path-critical preparation, not the target value constructor.
The 44 slot config rows are near-identical; only the instance selected at slot 23 produces the observed token. Non-selected reducer instances and the x/* decoy modules are off-chain.
Non-target reservation shadow.action console objects emitted during the same interaction (p0) are decoys and do not feed the target req_sig field.
oracle_notes.span_normalization: normalized_sha256 = sha256(slice with all /\s+/ runs collapsed to single spaces and trimmed). sha256 = sha256 of the exact captured byte slice [start_offset, end_offset).
debug_hints_private: The primary anchor is the inner signing closure returned by the exported factory u(config); in the captured bundle it is the function whose body contains the constant 0x27d4eb2d and the Math.imul/rotate signing loop.
The target field name req_sig and the action reservation.sign are assembled from character-code arrays at the sink.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default answer space.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to the captured signing closure (the anchor) returned by the factory.
Returned span maps to the target-specific signing-source builder (createSource) reached only through the anchor.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the signing path (makePlainMap, segment or r32).
Returned span maps to a path-critical slot-selection/factory function, the orchestrator or the console sink wrapper.
Returned span maps to a generic char-code/tuple/field/DOM helper used in preparation or sink packaging.
Returned span maps to an off-chain decoy (shadow emitter, non-selected reducer, x/* module) or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
